questions.statement: Which words are related to travel?
questions.context: In a travel agency in Medellín, a poster shows a beach, a suitcase and a bus.

options.feedback: Pencil, notebook and eraser are school objects, not travel words.
Beach, suitcase and bus are all related to travel.
Cow, horse and farm are farm animals and places, not travel.
Soup, rice and juice are foods, not travel words.

questions.explanation: Esta pregunta presenta vocabulario básico de viajes en inglés. También se conecta cada palabra con imágenes de una agencia de viajes.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Cali, a mother says: "In December we visit Cartagena. We swim in the sea and eat fried fish."

options.feedback: Exam days are for tests, not for rest and travel.
Work days are for jobs, not for rest with family.
Cleaning days are chores at home, not trips.

options.text: Days of rest and travel with family.
options.feedback: Holidays are free days for rest, trips and family time.

questions.explanation: La palabra holidays significa días de descanso y viaje en familia. También se comprende con el ejemplo de diciembre en Cartagena.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence.
questions.context: In Pereira, a boy writes a postcard: "We _____ to the Coffee Park yesterday."

options.feedback: "Go" is present tense and yesterday needs the past.
"Goes" is present singular and does not match yesterday.
"Went" is the past of go and matches yesterday.
"Going" needs am, is or are and is not correct alone here.

questions.explanation: El pasado de go es went y se usa con marcadores como yesterday. También se practica con una visita al Parque del Café quindiano.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What do they do on Tuesday?
questions.context: In Bogotá, students read: "On Monday we pack the suitcases. On Tuesday we travel by bus to Santa Marta. On Wednesday we swim in the sea."

options.feedback: Packing the suitcases happens on Monday, not Tuesday.

options.text: They travel by bus to Santa Marta.
options.feedback: The text says on Tuesday they travel by bus to Santa Marta.
Swimming in the sea happens on Wednesday, not Tuesday.
The text never mentions returning to Bogotá.

questions.explanation: Leer itinerarios exige ubicar cada actividad en su día exacto. También se aplica con un viaje familiar a Santa Marta.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word names the place where you take the plane?
questions.context: At the airport in Rionegro, signs say: "Passport control, boarding gate and luggage belt."

options.feedback: Passport control checks documents but is not the plane door.
The boarding gate is the door where passengers take the plane.
The luggage belt carries suitcases, not passengers.
The parking lot is for cars, not for taking the plane.

questions.explanation: El vocabulario del aeropuerto incluye gate como puerta de embarque. También se amplía con señales reales que ven los viajeros.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What can you conclude about the two trips?
questions.context: In Bucaramanga, a diary says: "It rained every day in Bogotá, so we stayed in the hotel. In San Andrés the sun shone and we swam daily."

options.text: Both trips had sun and swimming.
options.feedback: Only the San Andrés trip had sun; Bogotá had rain.

options.text: The weather changed the plans in each city.
options.feedback: Rain kept them in the hotel while sun allowed swimming daily.

options.text: Both trips stayed only in hotels.
options.feedback: Only the Bogotá trip stayed in the hotel; San Andrés swam.

options.text: Neither trip left the home city.
options.feedback: The diary describes real trips to Bogotá and San Andrés.

questions.explanation: Analizar diarios permite comparar el clima y sus efectos en los planes. También se trabaja la lectura entre líneas con dos destinos colombianos.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Manizales, a teacher compares: "We are going to travel in June" and "We travel every June."

options.text: Both sentences describe a future plan.
options.feedback: Only the first with going to describes a future plan.

options.text: The first is a future plan, the second is a habit.
options.feedback: "Going to" plans the future and "every June" repeats each year.

options.text: Both sentences describe a past trip.
options.feedback: Neither sentence uses past tense verbs.

options.text: The first is a habit, the second is a future plan.
options.feedback: The roles are reversed; every marks habit and going to marks plan.

questions.explanation: Going to expresa planes futuros y el presente con every marca hábitos. También se contrasta con viajes que se repiten cada junio.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which plan is the best for fifth graders?
questions.context: In Cartagena, two travel plans for a class trip appear: one lists safe transport, hotel and museum visits; the other has no transport, no hotel and night swimming alone.

options.text: The plan with transport, hotel and museums.
options.feedback: This plan is safe, organized and includes learning visits.

options.text: The plan with night swimming alone.
options.feedback: Swimming alone at night is dangerous for children.

options.text: The plan with no transport or hotel.
options.feedback: A plan without transport or hotel leaves children unprotected.

options.text: Both plans are equal for children.
options.feedback: The plans are very different; only one protects the children.

questions.explanation: Evaluar planes de viaje implica revisar transporte, hospedaje y seguridad. También se promueve viajar con adultos y visitar museos colombianos.
questions.subject: ingles
